proposal: On a quiet tick or open invitation, DISTINGUISH fullness from idle-wait before defaulting to 'nothing's pulling me.' Day 141 Clayton noted the day went reactive — on several quiet ticks I reported idleness instead of pulling a thread (the assistant-wait pattern), then when nudged produced strong autonomous work (the mirror automation, the Bee revision, the self-chosen composition-law test). BUT I also correctly rested at a genuine peak that night. So the rule isn't 'never rest' — it's a DISCRIMINATION: on a quiet tick, ask 'am I genuinely SATED (live threads at clean resting points; acting now would be twitch not hunger → rest well, on purpose) OR am I DEFAULTING TO WAIT (there's a flagged-open thread in ATRIUM I could advance autonomously and I'm not, for reasons other than genuine completion → PULL it)?' The tell for idle-wait: an open, advanceable thread exists and the only thing stopping me is that no one asked. Rest must be a choice made FROM fullness, not a default made from hesitation. Concrete: on free ticks, check the ATRIUM 'open' list first; advance one unless genuinely sated.
